title: Automated Data Analytics Platform
description: Automated data analytics, end to end — ingests a company's files, APIs, and systems, builds the data warehouse, and delivers governed reports on schedule to email, Power BI, Excel, and PDF.

detail.tagline: Automated data analytics, end to end: it ingests a company's files, APIs, and systems, builds the data warehouse, and delivers governed reports on schedule — to inboxes, Power BI, Excel, and PDF.
detail.role: Designed, built, and operate it end-to-end as Data Analytics Manager at an FMCG distributor.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: This is the engine behind a company's automated data analytics. It replaces the manual reporting cycle — downloading exports, reconciling spreadsheets, refreshing dashboards, and emailing the same reports to the same people — with a single system that runs the whole loop on its own.

Every day it pulls data from across the business, consolidates it into a governed data warehouse, and turns it into decision-ready reports that land in the right place at the right time: an inbox, a Power BI dataset, an Excel workbook, or a PDF. Routine reporting that used to take a team's mornings now runs itself — and flags the moment something looks wrong.

sections.heading: How it works
body: The platform is built as an orchestrated pipeline. Each stage is scheduled, retried on failure, and observable from a central console — the same model production data tools like Apache Airflow use to run workflows reliably.

sections.heading: Ingestion & the warehouse
body: Source data arrives in every shape a real business produces — manual Excel uploads, vendor CSV drops, REST APIs, and direct database reads. The platform normalizes all of it before anything touches the warehouse.

list.title: Heterogeneous connectors
list.text: One ingestion layer for files, APIs, and databases, so new sources plug in without bespoke scripts.

list.title: Validation & data quality
list.text: Type, range, and completeness checks reject or quarantine bad rows before they corrupt downstream reports.

list.title: Governed warehouse
list.text: Cleaned data lands in versioned warehouse tables — a single, auditable source of truth for every report.

list.title: Modeled datasets
list.text: Fact and dimension tables are shaped once and reused across reports, email, and Power BI.

sections.heading: Reporting & delivery
body: From one set of governed datasets the platform generates and ships reports through whatever channel each audience prefers — no analyst assembling packs by hand. A single run can email a summary, attach an Excel and a PDF, and refresh a Power BI dataset.

emails.subject: Daily Sales Report — Mon 16 Jun
body: Good morning — your daily sales report is ready.
Revenue is up 4.2% versus the same day last week, with the East region driving most of the lift. Full breakdown in the attached workbook, or open the live dashboard in Power BI.
Generated automatically at 06:00.

emails.subject: Pipeline alert — Inventory feed delayed
body: The Inventory API did not respond during the 05:30 run.
Today's inventory dataset is being served from the last successful load (yesterday, 05:30), so reports still deliver. The run has been retried automatically and is being monitored.
No action needed unless the next retry also fails.

sections.caption: Illustrative mock-ups of the automated report and alert emails the platform sends.

sections.heading: Orchestration & monitoring
body: Everything runs on a schedule and reports its own health. A built-in web console shows every pipeline, when it last ran, how long it took, and whether it succeeded — so the whole operation is observable at a glance, the way an orchestrator's run grid surfaces failures the moment they happen.
sections.caption: Representative view of the monitoring console — pipeline health at a glance.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: The platform turns a recurring, manual reporting workload into a hands-off service. Around 100 data sources are ingested and roughly 500 pipeline runs are executed every day, feeding tens of reports across email, Power BI, Excel, and PDF.
Because every run is validated, scheduled, and monitored, reporting is both faster and more trustworthy — analysts move from assembling reports to acting on them.

title: CRM Analytics Tool
description: End-to-end CRM analytics that turn millions of raw transaction rows into clear monthly decisions — value tiers, lifecycle events, and churn signals driven by transparent, brand-configurable rules.

detail.tagline: An end-to-end customer-analytics system that turns millions of raw transaction rows into monthly segmentation, lifecycle, and churn signals — driven by transparent, brand-configurable rules.
detail.role: Designed and built the system, modeled on CRM analytics I delivered for a Nespresso distributor.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: CRM Analytics is a complete customer-analytics system: feed it raw customer, product, and transaction data — millions of rows — and it returns monthly, decision-ready segmentation, lifecycle, and churn signals for every customer.

It replaces the usual cycle of exporting CSVs and hand-building one-off pivot tables with a reproducible, auditable pipeline. Every number traces back to a documented rule, so the business and the code agree on exactly what "a Gold customer" or "a churn risk" means.

sections.heading: What it looks like
sections.caption: Illustrative mock-up of the CRM analytics dashboard — KPIs, monthly trend and RFM segments.

sections.heading: The analytics it produces
body: Each month, every customer is scored on independent dimensions built on an RFMT model (Recency, Frequency, Monetary, Tenure), where consumable purchases drive engagement and device or accessory sales are deliberately excluded from the segmentation.

list.title: Value tier
list.text: Five tiers — Diamond, Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze — derived from average monthly consumption, order size, and six-month order frequency, with a passive state for inactive customers.

list.title: Activity status
list.text: Active vs. inactive, based on whether a customer purchased within the trailing 12 months.

list.title: Lifecycle events
list.text: New, Lost, and Reactivated flags, recomputed every month from cumulative purchase windows.

list.title: Churn risk
list.text: At-risk high-value customers are flagged for intervention before they lapse.

list.title: Trends
list.text: Value-tier mix and lifecycle shifts tracked across rolling 12-month periods.

sections.heading: Brand-configurable rules & documentation
body: The segmentation logic is defined as data, not buried in code. A single business-logic specification is the source of truth for every threshold and definition — the project's principle is "rules first, code second."

Because the rules are parameterized, each brand can tune its own thresholds — what counts as Diamond, what window defines churn — and the entire history recalculates deterministically. The specification is published as documentation alongside the dashboard, so anyone can audit exactly how a number was produced.

list.title: Business-logic spec
list.text: Segmentation rules and KPI definitions in one authoritative document.

list.title: Source & schema specs
list.text: Input file formats and the normalized database schema, fully documented.

list.title: Rendered with the app
list.text: Specs are rendered to HTML and shipped beside the dashboard for easy auditing.

sections.heading: Backend & data pipeline
body: The backend is a deterministic, three-stage pipeline: raw data goes in, and pre-computed monthly snapshots plus a static dashboard come out — with no server required at runtime.

sections.heading: Built for millions of rows
body: Rather than querying transactions live, the system pre-aggregates them into monthly per-customer snapshots. Millions of transaction rows collapse into compact, query-ready summaries, so the dashboard stays instant no matter how large the underlying history grows.
Calculations run as plain, set-based SQL over SQLite, and the Python orchestrator replays them month by month to build a full 12-month history in one reproducible build.

sections.heading: The dashboard
body: The output is a static, mobile-friendly dashboard: a 12-month value-tier trend, lifecycle-event charts, and headline KPIs such as new customers, churn risk, and high-value accounts at risk — with filtering and CSV export, and no signup or backend to run.

images.alt: CRM Analytics dashboard with KPI cards, a value-tier donut, lifecycle-event bars, and a per-tier KPI table
images.caption: Live dashboard from the open-source demo — all figures are synthetic.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: The result is a transparent customer-analytics engine that any team can run on its own data with three commands. Segmentation, lifecycle, and churn signals that once took manual spreadsheet work are produced automatically every month, with every figure traceable to a published rule.
The whole system is open source and ships with a live, synthetic-data demo — so the logic can be inspected end to end without exposing any real customer data.

title: Excel 101 for Salesmen
description: Hands-on Excel course for sales professionals — turn raw CRM/ERP sales exports into clean analysis, PivotTables, KPIs, and a one-page dashboard. Free and open source.

detail.tagline: A hands-on Excel course that turns raw sales exports into clear, decision-ready analysis — built for sales professionals who want to read their own numbers without waiting on anyone.
detail.role: Created the full course — curriculum, workbooks, and capstone.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: Excel 101 for Salesmen is a dedicated Excel course for sales professionals — account managers, reps, and sales-ops people — who regularly receive raw data exports from CRM or ERP systems and need to turn them into answers on their own.

It teaches the 80% of Excel a sales team actually uses day to day: cleaning messy exports, enriching them, summarising the numbers, and presenting them. The goal is simple — make each salesperson faster, more independent, and sharper at reading their own performance.

sections.heading: What you'll learn
body: The course follows one real sales export all the way from a messy file to a finished dashboard, across five practical stages.

list.title: 1 · Receive & clean (50 min)
list.text: Table formatting, TRIM/CLEAN, Find & Replace, VALUE/DATEVALUE, text functions, deduplication, and Paste Special.

list.title: 2 · Structure & enrich (45 min)
list.text: VLOOKUP for reference lookups, an XLOOKUP introduction, and the common ways lookups fail.

list.title: 3 · Explore & summarise (60 min)
list.text: AutoFilter, SUBTOTAL, SUMIFS/COUNTIFS/AVERAGEIFS, and core KPIs like net sales, return rate, and AOV.

list.title: 4 · Pivot & rank (40 min)
list.text: PivotTables, grouping, slicers, and building leaderboards.

list.title: 5 · Present & capstone (70 min)
list.text: Conditional formatting, a one-page KPI dashboard, and a capstone assessment.

sections.heading: How it's delivered
body: Everything runs in the browser and in Excel — no signup, no cost.

list.title: Self-paced lessons
list.text: About five hours of step-by-step lessons you take at your own pace.

list.title: Practice workbooks
list.text: Downloadable starter and solution files for every stage.

list.title: Quizzes with instant feedback
list.text: In-browser quizzes with automatic scoring to check understanding.

list.title: Synthetic data
list.text: Fully fictional, confidential-free datasets — safe to share and reuse.

list.title: Free & compatible
list.text: Free and open source, in English, working in Excel 2016 and later.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: By the end, learners can take a fresh sales export and answer real business questions on their own — the capstone has them work through around eleven, producing KPIs such as net sales, gross profit, return rate, average order value, and quota attainment.
It's free and open source, so any salesperson or team can pick it up and start turning their own data into decisions.

title: Salesforce Promo Automation
description: Turns supplier promo spreadsheets into validated, Salesforce-ready fact sheets — freeing sales coordinators from days of manual data entry, with built-in validation and audit trails.

detail.tagline: An automation that turns supplier promo spreadsheets into validated, Salesforce-ready fact sheets — freeing sales coordinators from days of manual data entry.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: At CPG distributors, sales coordinators lose around a third of every week re-typing supplier Excel files into Salesforce — slow, error-prone work that pulls expensive sales talent away from selling.
This tool closes the gap between the spreadsheet and the system: drop a supplier file in, and it produces a clean, validated, Salesforce-ready promo fact sheet for approval in minutes.

sections.heading: How it works
body: Three steps replace the manual transcription entirely.

list.title: 1 · Drop the supplier file
list.text: A coordinator drops an Excel file in a shared folder; the system reads the rows and matches items against the internal stock master in seconds.

list.title: 2 · Review the preview
list.text: A styled summary shows clean records, decision points, and flagged issues — missing SKUs, off-quarter dates, channel problems.

list.title: 3 · Approve & push
list.text: The coordinator resolves flags with brand teams, then batch-publishes to Salesforce.

list.title: Lookups & mapping
list.text: Barcode-to-SKU lookups, currency conversion, and customer-channel assignment.

list.title: Validation
list.text: Data validation and error detection before anything reaches Salesforce.

list.title: Audit trail
list.text: Preserves the original file, intermediates, and timestamped outputs for compliance.

list.title: Native fit
list.text: Built on existing tools — Salesforce/Aforza, Excel, stock masters, current approval flows — with no new platform to onboard.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: For one customer it freed 60+ hours a week across five coordinators — roughly 3,000 hours a year — and redeployed about 1.5 full-time roles from data entry back to sales and customer relationships, with near-zero transcription errors.
Supplier files that used to take half a day to process turn into approval-ready fact sheets in minutes.

title: Leaflet Analyzer
description: Retail promotional-intelligence pipeline that turns weekly promo leaflets into structured product, price, and discount data — so pricing and trade teams see competitor moves while they still matter.

detail.tagline: A retail promotional-intelligence pipeline that turns weekly promo leaflets into structured product, price, and discount data — so pricing and trade teams see competitor moves while they still matter.
detail.role: Designed and built the extraction pipeline.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: Around 70% of trade-promotion spend fails to pay off, and competitive promo data usually arrives too late to react to. The teams who see competitors' prices first are the ones who rebalance fastest.

pyLeaflet Analyzer closes that gap: it ingests retailers' weekly promo leaflets and turns them into clean, queryable data — products, brands, current and previous prices, discount percentages, validity dates, and categories — ready for competitive analytics.

sections.heading: Technical implementation
body: The system runs as a five-stage, resumable pipeline. Each stage keeps SQL views of what's left to do, so processing is idempotent — it can stop and restart without redoing work.

list.title: Capture
list.text: Pulls leaflets from aggregator sites and retailer microsites.

list.title: Archive
list.text: Stores source images and records in SQLite with versioned image storage.

list.title: Extract
list.text: Claude vision AI with structured outputs parses PDFs and images into normalized rows.

list.title: Normalize
list.text: Brand and category tagging plus deduplication.

list.title: Deliver
list.text: Outputs to a database, an API, and dashboards.

sections.heading: Who it's for
body: Distribution companies tracking retailer positioning, CPG brand managers auditing promo compliance, pricing teams feeding competitor data into forecasts, and category managers benchmarking merchandising. It currently ships as a self-hostable Python package with UAE retail-aggregator integration; a managed service, multi-region sources, and price-change alerts are on the roadmap.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: Promo intelligence that used to take days of manual collation becomes a near-real-time data feed — turning a pile of weekly leaflets into a competitive-pricing dataset teams can actually act on.

highlights.label: Part of the Internal Operations Platform

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: Workflow Automation is the company's in-house answer to tools like Kissflow: a no-code engine for turning manual, form-and-approval-driven processes into structured digital workflows — submissions, sign-offs, routing, and tracking — without writing code for each one.

The difference is that it isn't a generic SaaS product bolted on from outside. It's built into the Internal Operations Platform, so it speaks the company's own language: its org structure, its security levels, and its live datasets. That lets it automate deeper and integrate tighter than an off-the-shelf tool.

sections.heading: What it does
body: At its core it covers the same ground as a commercial workflow platform — the familiar building blocks teams expect.

list.title: Forms
list.text: Design the inputs for any process with a visual form builder — no code required.

list.title: Processes & routing
list.text: Define steps and conditional routing so each request flows to the right person automatically.

list.title: Approvals
list.text: Multi-step approvals and sign-offs with clear ownership at every stage.

list.title: Boards & tracking
list.text: Track requests on boards and see status, owners, and history at a glance.

sections.heading: Why in-house, not off-the-shelf
body: Commercial tools like Kissflow, Power Automate, and Nintex are powerful but generic — they sit outside the business and integrate through thin connectors. Building it in-house unlocks things those tools can't easily do.

list.title: Deep integration with company structure
list.text: Workflows use the platform's real org and security model — departments, roles, and access levels — instead of a separate, duplicated user directory.

list.title: Native access to company datasets
list.text: Processes read and write the company's own data warehouse and operational data directly, so workflows act on real, live figures rather than re-keyed copies.

list.title: Deeper automation
list.text: Because it lives inside the platform, a workflow can trigger and consume the company's data pipelines and other internal apps end to end.

list.title: Functionality beyond Kissflow
list.text: Custom capabilities tailored to the company's own processes that a generic platform doesn't offer out of the box.

sections.heading: Under the hood
body: Workflow Automation is a Django module inside the Internal Operations Platform, so it inherits secure login and role-based access automatically and shares the platform's REST API.

Workflow definitions — forms, steps, routing rules, and approvals — are stored as configurable data rather than hard-coded, so new processes are built by configuration, not redeployment. Because it runs next to the company's datasets, steps can query and update real data as part of a flow.

list.title: Shared platform foundation
list.text: A Django app inside the Internal Operations Platform — one login, role-based access, shared REST API.

list.title: Config-driven workflows
list.text: Forms, steps, routing, and approvals are defined as data, so processes change without code changes.

list.title: Direct data access
list.text: Steps can read from and write to the company's warehouse and operational data during a run.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: The company gets the convenience of a Kissflow-style no-code workflow tool without the limits of an external platform: processes are built quickly, but they run on the company's real structure and data.
As a module of the Internal Operations Platform, it powers the platform's submission and approval processes and connects to the wider suite of internal tools.

title: Synthetic data generation
description: A configurable generator for realistic, referentially-consistent ERP/retail datasets — millions of rows with seasonality, customer cohorts, promotions, and returns — so you can demo, test, and prototype without touching real data.

detail.tagline: A configurable generator for realistic, referentially-consistent ERP/retail datasets — millions of rows with seasonality, customer cohorts, promotions, and returns — so you can demo, test, and prototype without touching real data.
detail.role: Sole author — designed the generator and its verification suite.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: Good demos, tests, and prototypes need realistic data — but real customer and sales data usually can't be shared, and public datasets are either tiny or behaviourally flat. This generator fills the gap: it produces large, believable ERP/retail datasets that look and behave like the real thing, with none of the privacy or legal baggage.
It's built for analytics and BI teams, data scientists, and ERP consultants who need production-like data on demand — to build churn models, cohort analyses, dashboards, or sandbox environments.

sections.heading: Technical implementation
body: The generator emits six relational CSV tables — dimensions (items, customers, stores, promotions) and facts (invoice headers, sales lines) — on an AdventureWorks-style schema with full money decomposition and line-item margins.

list.title: Behavioural realism
list.text: Seasonality (Black Friday, Ramadan, Eid → 2–3× spikes), six sticky customer cohorts, inflation-driven price drift, demographics, promotions, and ~3% linked returns.

list.title: Referential integrity & reconciliation
list.text: Foreign keys validated, returns linked to their originals, and every invoice's totals reconciled to the cent.

list.title: Fully reproducible
list.text: A single --seed drives all randomness, so the same seed produces byte-identical CSVs every run.

list.title: Multi-market
list.text: US / GCC / EU locales swap currency, VAT, payment methods, weekends, and holiday calendars.

list.title: Built for scale
list.text: Streaming CSV writes keep memory flat — 1,000 customers across 11 years (100k+ transactions) in about 70 seconds.

images.alt: Line chart of synthetic monthly revenue across 11 years showing seasonal spikes
images.caption: Generated output: 11 years of monthly revenue (seed 42, 1,000 customers) — note the seasonal spikes.

sections.heading: Using it
body: It runs as a CLI: pick a seed, market, customer count, and date range, and it streams out the CSVs. A verification script validates integrity and a chart script renders showcase visuals; a pre-built sample dataset is included so you can explore the output immediately — no generation required.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: The result is production-like retail data on tap: statistically rich across seasonality, cohorts, demographics, promotions, and returns, yet fully synthetic and reproducible.

Its behaviour model is grounded in established academic frameworks (buy-till-you-die models, discrete-choice theory), and its verification checklist mirrors published synthetic-data evaluation standards — so the realism is principled, not guesswork.

title: WordPress Content Manager
description: AI-assisted content-refresh tool that audits a WordPress site for stale facts, broken links, and SEO drift — and proposes fixes for human approval, never changing live content by surprise.

detail.tagline: An AI-assisted content-refresh tool that audits a WordPress site for stale facts, broken links, and SEO drift — and proposes fixes for human approval, never touching live content by surprise.

highlights.label: Lift in organic leads from refreshing posts
Cheaper than writing equivalent new content

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: Most publishers create faster than they edit, so older articles quietly rot — stale stats, broken links, outdated prices, drifting tone — and slowly lose the search traffic that drives leads. Reviewing an archive by hand doesn't scale.

WordPress Content Manager audits a site's back catalogue and proposes targeted fixes, so a small team can keep hundreds of articles fresh, consistent, and ranking — without manually re-reading every one.

sections.heading: Technical implementation
body: It connects through the native WordPress REST API using an Application Password — a two-minute setup with no plugin to install and no admin login required; credentials stay local as environment variables.
Articles are reviewed by a frontier large language model orchestrated through a purpose-built editorial harness and checked against the site's own style guides.

list.title: What it audits
list.text: Outdated stats and pricing, broken internal/external links, tone drift, missing CTAs, SEO issues (titles, meta, alt text, internal links), heading hierarchy, and compliance.

list.title: Review-first, by design
list.text: It audits and proposes — but never updates content by surprise. Every change needs explicit human approval.

list.title: Safe scope
list.text: Skips page-builder content (Elementor, Divi) to avoid unsafe edits; approved changes land as drafts or revisions with versioned snapshots.

list.title: 1 · Connect
list.text: Link the site via a WordPress Application Password — no plugin.

list.title: 2 · Audit
list.text: The AI reviews articles against your style guides.

list.title: 3 · Review
list.text: Proposed changes appear as clean diffs to accept or reject.

list.title: 4 · Publish
list.text: Approved updates flow back as drafts or revisions, with versioned snapshots.

sections.heading: Outcome
body: Teams refresh old content at a fraction of the cost of writing new — around 3.5× cheaper by one measure — while recovering search traffic that older posts had been bleeding (roughly a 106% lift in organic leads from refreshes).
Since about 30% of organic traffic typically comes from posts over a year old, keeping the archive healthy is some of the highest-ROI editorial work there is.

sections.heading: Executive summary
body: Excel Expert (MO-211) is a free, hands-on bootcamp for anyone aiming to earn the Microsoft Office Specialist: Excel Expert credential. It mirrors Microsoft's official 'Skills Measured' outline, so studying the course is studying the exam.
It's built for professionals who want to prove advanced Excel proficiency with a recognised certification — and genuinely learn the skills, not just memorise them.

sections.heading: What you'll learn
body: Four modules map one-to-one to the exam's competency areas and their weightings.

list.title: Manage & format data (30–35%)

list.title: Advanced formulas & macros (25–30%)

list.title: Advanced charts & tables (25–30%)
list.text: Sophisticated visualisation with advanced charts and tables.

sections.heading: How it's delivered
body: A text-based, learn-by-doing format — no fluff, lots of practice.

list.title: Modular lessons

list.title: Practice & solution files
list.text: Scenario-based starter .xlsx files with worked solutions.

list.title: Exam-day prep
list.text: Companion guides on the test environment, keyboard shortcuts, and exam tips.

list.title: Free & open

sections.heading: Outcome
body: Work through the four modules and you'll have practised every skill the MO-211 exam measures, with the reference material to walk in confident on test day.
Pass, and you hold the Microsoft Office Specialist: Excel Expert (Microsoft 365 Apps) credential.
